reference.title: The screens of the app
reference.shortdesc: What each place in the list on the left shows, what the top of every screen holds, and what the More list opens.

section.title: The list on the left
section.p: A list of five places runs down the left side of every screen, whichever way up you hold the iPad. The place you are in is shaded. Some places show your whole tree. Others show one person, the person named in the chip that starts with . The chip shows once you open someone.

table.title: The places in the list and what they show

row.entry: The tree that is open, with a search box and the people you opened last.
The page of one person. On its side, the iPad shows the family tree beside it.
A drawing of the person with parents, partners and children.
The things that happened in that person's life.
A list of other places, such as your trees, your notes and the colours.

section.note: If a page says Select a person or shows only the search box, it needs a person first. Search for someone, then open them. shows how.

section.title: The top of every screen
section.p: A line at the top names the tree and the page you are on. Choose a name in that line to go back to that page. A back arrow at the top left takes you back one screen. Below the line are three buttons.

ul.li: , with a magnifying glass, opens the search. It is not on , because has a search box of its own.
opens the sheet that adds something new. shows it.
, with a question mark, opens the guide to the screen you are on in the web browser of your iPad.

section.p: Every field of a form also has a small help button of its own.

This is the first screen. It names the tree that is open and counts its people, families and events. It has a search box, two buttons and, once you have opened people, the names you can go back to. shows how to search.

ul.li: lists the people you opened last.

section.p: This is one person's page: their names, their birth and death, their family and their photos. With the iPad on its side, the page is in two parts. The person is on the left, and their is on the right, with its own buttons. Drag the divider between the two parts to make one wider. shows how to open a person.

section.title: The list
section.p: Choose to see eight places. Each one opens a screen of its own, with a line under its heading that says what it is for.

ul.li: lists your family trees, one card for each.
shows your own notes about the person you are looking at. shows how to write one.
lists the archives, libraries and websites that your sources come from. shows how to add one.
lists the people credited with the tree.
is your list of questions and ideas. shows how to add one.

shows the version of the app.

section.p: The lists for the whole tree are empty until you add something with .

section.title: Your trees
section.p: Choose in the list. Each card is one family tree. It tells you how many people, families and events the tree holds, and which tree is . On its side, the iPad shows two cards to a row.

section.title: When the iPad is upright
section.p: The pictures in this manual show the iPad on its side. Upright, the screen is narrower, and some screens change.

ul.li: The list on the left stays.
A person's page does not have the family tree beside it. Choose to see the tree.
The forms are in one column. is further down, so scroll to find it.
The cards on are one under another.
